newsitem.title: UK: Freschi & Schiavoni invest 5bn lira in terminal.
newsitem.headline: Freschi & Schiavoni invest 5bn lira in terminal.

text.p: Privately-owned Italian trucking company, Freschi & Schiavoni, has invested five billion Italian lira in a new cargo terminal, near to Milan Linate International Airport, a company spokeswoman said.
The new terminal has a total surface area of 13,000 sq m, with 4,000 sq m of warehousing and 14 truck docking stations.
Nearly half of the new premises are reserved for Swissair which has already moved into the new premises, which are eight km from the Italian airport.

Commenting on the move, Chris Heiz, general manager Swissair Cargo Italy, said: "The ever-growing demand for cargo capacity out of northern Italy saturated the capacity of the facilities we had put in operation in 1988"
Export traffic trucked from Milan to Switzerland has risen from 10,000 tons in 1990, to an estimated 24,000 tons by the end of this year, he said.
Managing director of the trucking company, Betty Schiavoni, said the company would now be able to increase its share of the air cargo traffic handled from Italy to other European airports.
Freschi & Schiavoni has had a partnership with Swissair for 26 years.
The trucking company also handles traffic for Singapore Airlines, Korean Airlines, Malaysia Airlines and United Airlines.
With a fleet of 35 trailers, it offers services from Liscate to Milan, Frankfurt, Brussels, Amsterdam, as well as the three major Swiss airports.
The trucking company is a family run operation established in 1962 and it now employs 70 people. It also has premises in Bologna, Florence and Rome.
